doc:
Which body copy the TradFi-perps risk-disclosure sheet renders.

Deliberately a VARIANT ENUM rather than a Rust-emitted `pr_*` CDKey: a Rust-emitted key must be
registered in BOTH Kotlin resolution cache tables, and a miss in one renders the raw key while a
miss in the other renders an empty string — on a compliance screen. Emitting a variant instead
keeps no key crossing the FFI boundary, so neither table needs an entry. Native maps the variant
to its own `R.string`.

There is intentionally NO third "unresolved" variant. The readiness fallback (FR-2-AC-3) resolves
an unavailable feature-restriction fact to [`Self::Standard`] inside Rust, so every value Native
can ever observe is already a real decision. Native therefore never needs a
placeholder-versus-resolved predicate, and cannot accidentally treat the default variant as
"not yet known".

name: TradeSessionHandle
doc:
Opaque cross-crate / cross-FFI handle to the trade session.

This exists solely so another crate's UniFFI factory (e.g. the retail-kline
K-line interactor) can receive the current session **without
`TradeSessionContext` itself crossing the FFI boundary or appearing on the
ABI**. Native holds it opaquely and passes it straight back into the
factory; it exposes no methods over FFI.

It wraps a `Weak`, so keeping the handle alive never pins the session past
its owning `MainTradeInteractor` (mirrors the child-interactor rule that the
session reference is always `Weak`). A dead `Weak` simply upgrades to `None`
and the consumer degrades gracefully.

Only `MainTradeInteractor::trade_session_handle` constructs this; there is
deliberately no `#[uniffi::constructor]`.

fields.name: price_raw
fields.doc:
Machine-readable twin of `price_text`: the value a depth tap fills.

Behavior Contract = Native `DepthP.kt:142 / :160`, which hands the widget's DISPLAY
price straight into `price.formatS()` (`com.okinc.core.ktx`, the numeric-sanitiser
family). So this is `price_text` with formatting stripped, which means:
* it IS the rounded price (bid down / ask up by `ladder_digits`), not the
pre-rounding `OKTFormattedDepthItem::un_format_price`;
* for the `<{ladder}` lower edge bucket (row price 0, amount != 0 -- the sentinel
label from `depth_batch_convertor.rs:186-188`, mirroring native
`DepthM.kt:123-126`) the sanitiser leaves the ladder number: tapping "<10" fills
10, exactly as native does. Same for the EVENTS ">{1-ladder}" upper bucket.

Why the field has to exist: `price_text` is a DISPLAY value and is NOT always a
number. Feeding it to the order panel verbatim put the literal "<10" in as a price --
it parses nowhere, so the option sheet's IV plus its available / max-buy / max-sell
rows collapsed to "--" and flickered (recvvCBHHRkTfd, reproduced by tapping the "<10"
row; a numeric row was fine). This is the price-axis counterpart of `amount_raw`
below, which exists for the same reason on the amount axis.

EMPTY means "no numeric price on this row at all", and the host's existing
`price.isEmpty()` click guard then makes the tap a no-op. The edge bucket is NOT such
a row -- it carries the ladder.

name: MultiSlEditFocusField
doc:
R1b — render-ready projection of the stop-loss leg currently being EDITED in
the V1 `MultipleSlSettingFragment` "set multiple SL" dialog.

# Why this is separate from `PureContractMultiTpEditProjection`
The SL setting dialog differs STRUCTURALLY from the TP one (this is not a
1:1 mirror of R1a — verified against V1, not assumed):
- **No percent / progress.** A MULTI batch has many TP legs that split the
position by percent (`MultipleTpSettingFragment` seek-bar + `calcEstimateAmount`
+ set/remaining/full progress), but exactly ONE stop-loss that closes the
FULL position (V1 `MultiSlDetailView.kt:82-93` renders the constant
"100%"). So there is no `estimate_amount` / `set_percent` / `left_percent` /
`is_full` here — those TP fields have no SL analog.
- **No fragment-local compute to move.** R1a migrated
`MultipleTpSettingFragment.calcEstimateAmount:374` (a Fragment-local
`TradeAvailableManager` A1 violation). `MultipleSlSettingFragment` has ZERO
local arithmetic — it delegates entirely to `UniSetTpSlView` / the shared
`mSlPresenter` (`AbsTpSlPresent`). The only render-time derived value the SL
edit form shows is the estimated PnL, which this projection owns so the
eventual Kotlin pure-ification reads Rust state instead of the shared
presenter (A1: Rust owns the compute).

# Single SSoT note — what is and isn't here
The SSoT inputs (`edit_sl_trigger_px` / `_ord_px` / `_is_limit_kind` /
`_is_cost_price` / `_trigger_px_type`) cover the **trigger-price input mode**
(worklog scope #2). The V1 4-input-type cross-derivation
(price-change / pnl-rate / pnl-amount / dynamic — `TP_SL_BY_PRICE_CHANGE` /
`_RATE` / `_PNL` / `_DYNAMIC`, deriving the trigger from a PnL-rate /
PnL-amount / price-change input) is NOT wired here: it lives in the shared
`mSlPresenter`, not in the
SL dialog, and porting it is a separate design-gated round (the
`attach_facade::calc_trigger_price_by_rate` / `_by_pnl_amount` calculators
already EXIST — A3: reported as deferred, not fabricated).

# V1 source map (MultipleSlSettingFragment.kt / UniSetTpSlView.kt)
- `estimate_pnl`     ← SL PnL at the SL effective price for the FULL position
(`calc_pnl_display_by_price`, the SAME ByPrice formula as the OCO reverse SL
+ R1a TP profit). Signed; typically negative (a triggered SL is a loss).
`Placeholder` when not derivable (no effective price / metadata not loaded /
non-derivative inst — A3: no fabrication).
- `trigger_px` / `ord_px` ← echo of `edit_sl_trigger_px` / `edit_sl_ord_px`.
- `is_limit_kind`    ← limit-order (xian-jia) checkbox (`isSlLimitCbChecked`,
`UniSetTpSlView.kt:435`). Distinct from `is_cost_price` (verified: separate
controls).
- `is_cost_price`    ← cost-price (cheng-jiao-jia) SL (`slSwitch` →
`AMEND_PX_ON_TRIGGER_TYPE_OPEN_PRICE` → `isOpenPriceSl()`,
`MultipleSlSettingFragment.kt:213/244`). Trigger == mother order price, so
the estimated PnL at break-even is ~0.
- `trigger_px_type`  ← `slTriggerType` (last / mark / index).
- `is_estimate_visible` ← whether `estimate_pnl` is derivable (V1 shows the
SL PnL bubble only when the trigger yields a value).

Bug A (device: empty trigger / empty limit-order price on confirm neither
focuses the box nor blocks) — which SL-edit input the confirm should focus
when it hard-blocks on an empty required field. Native
`OKTFuturesMultiSLModuleVC.m valueIsValid` / `MultipleSlSettingFragment`
`getSlPriceInfo(checkValid=true)`: empty trigger -> focus trigger; limit-order
checked + empty order-px -> focus order-px. `None` = valid / not blocked.
One-shot: set only by a blocked `on_multi_sl_edit_commit`, read once by the
dialog, reset to `None` by the next projection recompute.
